**Key passages in source vs. draft:**

1. "she wearies with her endless hill" — cut from draft
2. "my brain seems to beat against the solid metal; aye, steel skull, mine; the sort that needs no helmet in the most brain-battering fight!" — absent
3. "Dry heat upon my brow? Oh! time was, when as the sunrise nobly spurred me, so the sunset soothed. No more." — absent
4. The stage direction "waving his hand, he moves from the window" — absent (minor)
5. "Good night—good night!" — absent
6. "subtly and most malignantly" compressed to "most malignantly" — partial
7. "man has ye there" — absent from the swerve passage
8. The dramatic paragraph break and reordering: source has the "Good night" moment BEFORE the second soliloquy about the cogged circle; draft merges them out of order, placing the cogged-circle passage after the "I'm demoniac" line — this is a structural/interpretive reordering that matters for the dramatic arc (Ahab first moves from the window in farewell, then turns defiant).

The most critical losses:

- "Dry heat upon my brow? Oh! time was, when as the sunrise nobly spurred me, so the sunset soothed. No more." — this is the title chapter's thematic keystone.
- "steel skull, mine; the sort that needs no helmet in the most brain-battering fight!" — highly distinctive rhetoric
- "Good night—good night!" with the stage direction — interpretively significant break
